nodes.title: What is happening with your internet?
answers: Only one device has a problem

nodes.title: Look at the router. Are its lights on?
answers: Lights are on, some are red or orange

nodes.title: Check the power
nodes.text: Make sure the power cable is firmly connected to the router and to a working wall socket. Try another socket. If the router still shows no lights, it may need to be replaced.

nodes.title: Your provider may have an outage
nodes.text: A red or orange internet light usually means the router has no signal from your provider. Check that the cable from the wall is connected, then check your provider's outage page or call them.

nodes.title: Unplug the router, wait 30 seconds and plug it back in. Wait two minutes. Does it work now?
Great, you are back online
nodes.text: Restarting clears temporary faults. If you need to restart often, the router may be overheating; keep it in an open, ventilated spot.

nodes.title: Contact your internet provider
nodes.text: The router seems fine but there is no connection. Your provider can test the line from their side.

nodes.title: Is Wi-Fi turned on, and is airplane mode off on that device?
answers: I fixed that and it works
Both are fine, still no connection

nodes.title: Forget the network and reconnect
nodes.text: Open the Wi-Fi settings on the device, choose your network, select Forget, then connect again and re-enter the password. Restarting the device also helps.

nodes.title: Are you far from the router or behind thick walls?
answers: No, I am close to it

nodes.title: Move closer or add a mesh point
nodes.text: Wi-Fi gets weaker through walls and floors. Place the router in a central, raised spot, or add a mesh access point or extender.

nodes.title: Check what is using the connection
nodes.text: Large downloads, video streaming and backups on other devices can slow everyone down. Pause them and run a speed test. If the speed is far below your plan, contact your provider.
